classification.parent: Vocabulary > Word Pattern > Words Ending in -ill
classification.reason: This topic groups high-frequency words by shared spelling ending to improve recognition and production.

similarities: Both endings appear in common English words.
Both can occur in nouns and verbs.
Both may sound similar in fast speech.
differences: -ill words usually keep double l, such as skill, still, drill, and refill.
-il words have one l, such as pencil and civil.
A missing l can create frequent spelling errors at B1 level.
When unsure, verify the full word from memory or context, not only sound.

association.note: A practical grouping is: school learning (skill, drill), time logic (still, until), daily actions (refill), and places (hill).

counterExample.reason: The correct spelling is 'skill' with double l.

counterExample.wrong: Wait here intil I call you.
counterExample.reason: The correct word is 'until'. This error happens when learners write only by sound.
The correct form is 'refill' with double l.

scenario.description: Office: An intern improves report-writing skill through a weekly drill. School: Students stay still until the fire drill instructions end. Travel: Refill your bottle before hiking up the hill. Daily conversation: I am still busy until dinner. Academic writing: This study measures language skill over one term. Business email: We will review this procedure until all team members can do it without help.

mnemonic.content: For common target words like skill, still, drill, and refill, pause before punctuation and check if you wrote two l letters at the end.

confusion.confusedWith: -ill words vs similar-sound words with one l
confusion.reason: Learners often drop one l in spelling. Distinguish by storing high-frequency -ill words as chunks and checking them during proofreading.
